questions.knowledge_point: Identifying Regions Where a Function Is Positive or Negative Using a Sign Table
questions.problem:
Consider the expression $f(x,y)=(x-2)(y+1)^{2}.$  What are the missing entries in the sign table of $f(x,y),$ shown below?

| $y>-1$ |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<-1$ |  |  |
|  | $x<2$ | $x>2$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=2$ and $y=-1.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14065421/assets/a66a57932dbc935b5ed6f74b4f0faa0047c4b7ef58ded46be088dad30fa5eee4.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14065421/assets/52efe97fcffa3da05151b3ffef5305e0c3ec0d567d3f62b964a30740c08a3981.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $(x-2)$ | $(y+1)^{2}$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-left | $(-2,1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Top-Right | $(4,1)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(-2,-3)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(4,-3)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |

 

Using the *last* column of the table above, we get the following picture:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14065421/assets/aa100568c18b31507c775e77ed3201a5aed6f708b541e48046617a43fe9a8304.png)

Finally, we fill in the required sign table.

| $y>-1$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<-1$ | $-$ | $+$ |
|  | $x<2$ | $x>2$ |

questions.problem: Suppose that $f(x,y)=x(y+1).$ Which of the following shaded areas gives the solution to the inequality $f(x,y)\ge 0?$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=0$ and $y=-1.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below. Since we have an "or equal to" inequality, we use solid lines to divide the plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14065421/assets/599d3a551a20e68989e5de517711ae4c7c73255fb4a9d716797cf90dbb32a4ea.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14065421/assets/43bb5eac3414291bbd844a3608835a6f7be3e5e0dfcc2ae89426581eccdc87b3.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $x$ | $(y+1)$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-Left | $(-1,0)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Top-Right | $(1,0)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(-1,-2)$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(1,-2)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |

 

Finally, on our diagram, we shade in the solutions to $f(x,y)\ge 0$ using the *last* column of the table above.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14065421/assets/18757d46e86eb0d771841e7f5fe13be9ad464ccaf66b7190e7a2a7f02428a88e.png)
